literal_source_claim: The Cesaro means for a continuous function converge.
canonical_claim: For a continuous function on the circle, the first-order Cesaro means of its symmetric Fourier partial sums converge uniformly to the function.
domain_and_universes: T : Real with Fact (0 < T); f : C(AddCircle T, Complex); Cesaro index n : Nat; symmetric Fourier frequency j : Int; Prop in Lean universe 0.
quantifiers: continuous function f on AddCircle T
natural Cesaro index n tending to infinity
hypotheses: f is continuous, preferably represented as a bundled continuous map
conclusion: The mean of symmetric partial sums S_0 through S_n tends to f in the continuous-map topology (uniformly on the compact circle).
excluded_degenerate_cases: Nonpositive periods are excluded. Index zero is included and checked: S_0 contains frequency zero and the zeroth Fejer mean equals S_0. Constant and zero functions remain in scope. Real-valued and merely pointwise variants receive no statement credit.
